sources.title: Blombos Cave Ornaments
sources.author: Middle Stone Age Inhabitants
sources.excerpt: Shells pierced and strung, ochre-stained, the world's oldest jewelry, the first symbols of identity.
sources.longExcerpt: In Blombos Cave, South Africa, we find humanity's first art. Shells collected from the beach, carefully pierced with bone awls, strung on cord, stained with ochre. Seventy-five thousand years ago, someone wore these as a necklace. This is not survival but culture - the need to adorn, to signal identity, to be beautiful. Here too are ochre blocks engraved with geometric patterns, the earliest abstract art. Before we conquered the world, we conquered ourselves, becoming symbol-makers, meaning-seekers.
